newsitem.title: INDIA: Kazakh leader confident of end to India tea row.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh leader confident of end to India tea row.

text.p: Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev said on Monday he was confident Indian and Kazakh businessmen would settle a $7.6 million tea dispute.

Indian officials have accused a Kazakh state firm of failing to pay for tea imports worth $7.6 million in 1993, and said the row has threatened to spoil recently forged trade ties between the two countries.
"Those are the areas that come up once in a while between different companies," Nazarbayev told reporters after a ceremonial reception at Delhi's British-built presidential palace.
"Certainly there exists legislation and political law that should be used in their resolution."
Nazarbayev was asked if the two countries would resolve the dispute during his three-day visit.
"I believe the business people of India and Kazakhstan will be able to sort it out among themsleves. Besides, we are talking about small sums," the visiting leader said.
Indian ministers have frequently raised the issue with their Kazakh counterparts.
They have been assured that the Kazakh State Foreign Trade Company would find a way of paying for the tea, which it bought from India's Rassik Woodworth Ltd.

India was the main tea exporter to the former Soviet Union. It has been grappling with disputes over payments and the quality of exports with the Commonwealth of Independent States ever since the collapse of communist rule in Moscow.
